title: test(runtime): judge each share-link password pair once in the refusal-order file, so its loop cases fit the 5000 ms default
body:
Fixes #24633
Clause-②: no

## What changes

One test file: `packages/runtime/src/domains/share-links-refusal-order.test.ts`. Its `beforeAll` wraps the `ShareLinkService` instance's own password verifier in a memo keyed by the `(password, hash)` pair. The first request that presents a given pair is judged by the production verifier (scrypt at the account parameters). Every later request with the same pair replays that verdict.

What stays the same:
- Every request is still made. Every row of the table and every cell of the three loop cases' matrices is still asserted, against both mounts.
- The service is still built with both password members at their defaults, as production builds it, so its legacy-hash upgrade stays on. No row in this file is legacy.
- No case is skipped, quarantined, re-timed or re-asserted.
- No per-case timeout, no `testTimeout` change and no `// test-budget:` header.

The production verifier is not exported from `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, so the memo reads it off the instance. If that member is renamed, `beforeAll` throws with a message that names the member. It does not quietly fall back to paying for every call.

## Measured cause: production scrypt verifications, not the resolves

`resolveToken` calls the verifier once for each password presented to a live, password-protected link:
- on a `signed_in` link, once the caller is signed in;
- on an `email` link, whatever email was sent (the same-work rule from #23474).

Each call derives a scrypt key at N=16384, r=16. I counted the calls with a temporary instrumented copy of the file. The copy wrapped the instance's verifier and hasher with counters keyed by `expect.getState().currentTestName`. It was deleted after the run and never committed (`git status` clean after each run).

| | before (`eadea5720`) | after (`a70fd811f`) |
|:--|--:|--:|
| verifier calls per file run | 70 | 70 |
| ...of which reach the production scrypt verifier | 70 | **6** |
| mints with a password (`hashPassword`, in `beforeAll`) | 4 | 4 |
| **scrypt derivations per file run** | **74** | **10** |
| `:334` no-password-oracle loop (13 resolves), per mount | 8 | 0 |
| `:346` allowlist-membership loop (8 resolves), per mount | 4 | 0 |
| `:356` unknown-token loop (18 resolves), per mount | 10 | 0 |
| most derivations in any one case | 10 | 1 |

The 6 distinct pairs are the 3 live protected links (`signed_in + password`, `public + password`, `email + password`), each with a wrong password and with the correct one. The revoked link is refused before verification. A verdict depends only on its pair, so replaying it changes no answer.

## Readings

**CI, before.** Run `39298888283`:
- Attempt 1, job `118219765573` (`Test Core (6/6)`): the card's red. `:356`, dispatcher twin, failed with `Test timed out in 5000ms`.
- Attempt 2, job `118235895669`: green on the same head.
- The `Test Core` aggregate job `118247422913` prints the suite-ceiling report into its log. It lists this file as `@objectstack/runtime`'s slowest: `34.84s  src/domains/share-links-refusal-order.test.ts [local]`. That is over the 10 s line in AGENTS.md (Build & Test).
- The `test-core-timings-6-of-6` artifact could not be read from here. The artifact download redirects to blob storage, and this container's egress proxy answers that redirect 403.

**Local runs.** The box has 4 vCPUs and is shared with sibling agents. Every run took the verify lock. Durations come from vitest's JSON reporter. The "file" figure is vitest's module line for the file.

| reading | before (`eadea5720`) | after (`810176fb8`, `a70fd811f`) |
|:--|:--|:--|
| file, idle, `--maxWorkers=2` | 7778 / 7725 ms | 1330 / 1215 / 1296 ms |
| `:334`, idle (plugin route / twin) | 796, 779 / 819, 803 ms | 17, 15 / 14, 13 ms |
| `:346`, idle | 386, 410 / 398, 391 ms | 13, 8 / 8, 8 ms |
| `:356`, idle | 1148, 1024 / 966, 1024 ms | 20, 19 / 18, 18 ms |
| slowest case, idle | 1148 ms | 116 / 99 ms (a row with one fresh verification) |
| contention: the file pinned to CPU 3 beside 5 busy loops on CPU 3, `--maxWorkers=1` | **3 failed, `Test timed out in 5000ms`**: `:356` plugin route 5050 ms, `:356` twin 5002 ms, `:334` twin 5001 ms. `:334` plugin route passed at 4808 ms. File 44531 ms. | **60 passed**. File 8685 ms. Loop cases 72 to 169 ms. Slowest case 638 ms. |

Notes on these readings:
- The "before" contention run reproduces the card's failure shape on the card's case: a timeout, not an assertion. It also shows `:334` is the next case to go.
- The contention load is heavier than the CI shard that read 34.84 s: 44.53 s against 34.84 s, about 1.28x.
- The two runs taken after the change differ only in a comment and a named type alias. The idle reading at the final head, `a70fd811f`, is the third one (1296 ms).

**CI, after: NOT MEASURED** until this PR's `Test Core` runs. Two projections, both under 10 s:
- 5.5 to 6.0 s, from the idle figures and the before ratio of CI to idle (34.84 / 7.75, about 4.5x);
- about 6.8 s, from the contention figure divided by the contention-to-CI ratio (8685 ms / 1.28).

## Why not the suggested per-case timeout, and why there is no `test-budget` header

- **A per-case timeout leaves the file over the 10 s line.** It would keep 4 to 10 derivations inside each loop case, and the file would stay near 35 s in CI. AGENTS.md says a file over 10 s of wall is its lane's card, unless the file declares a measured budget with its class.
- **No class fits this file, so it cannot declare a budget.** `TEST_BUDGET_CLASSES` in `scripts/measure-test-shard-timings.mjs` is a closed list of three classes. Its reader refuses any other class:
  - `spawns the real producer once per single-cause fixture`;
  - `whole-package import`;
  - `compiles the package type graph once`.

  None of the three describes key derivations.
- **So the change removes the cost instead.** The file now projects under the line, and the loop cases no longer need a budget. The slowest case under contention read 638 ms, 12.8% of the 5000 ms default.
- **The precedents were read from their landed diffs.**
  - `b9222dc70` (#22426) sized per-case budgets for files whose subject is the hashing itself, and its rule was never to lower the scrypt parameters. That rule holds here: every verdict still comes from production scrypt at the production parameters.
  - `7b6c65290` (#21925, for #21920) moved a module load out of the clocked window. The shape does not transfer, because the cost here is the cases' own derivations.
  - #22356 has no landed diff to read. Its timeline's `closed` event carries no commit, and no commit on `origin/main` cites it. As a control, the same grep finds `b9222dc70` for #22426.

## Mechanism assumptions, checked

1. *"About 18 sequential resolves per loop case."* **Partly falsified.**
   - The three cases make 13, 8 and 18 resolves.
   - Their cost is the 8, 4 and 10 production scrypt verifications among those resolves. The same resolves now read 8 to 20 ms per whole case.
   - The contended-shard reading holds: attempt 2 passed on the same head.
2. *"The matrix is needed whole."* **Confirmed, and kept.** No cell is dropped.

## Tests and gates

All at `a70fd811f` (`git rev-parse --short HEAD`), the PR head.

- `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/runtime^...' build` under the verify lock: `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run --project local --maxWorkers=2 src/domains/share-links-refusal-order.test.ts`, under the lock: `Tests 60 passed (60)`, file line 1296 ms.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime typecheck`, under the lock: `VERDICT command-exit 0`. This includes `check:test-typecheck: OK`. The file is in `tsconfig.test.json`'s program: `tsc --listFilesOnly` counts it once.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` derived 53 commands. Results:
  - 51 exited 0.
  - 2 exited 3 (`PREREQUISITE NOT MET`), so they are NOT MEASURED here:
    - `node scripts/check-plugin-teardown-shape.mjs --self-test` needs an unshallowed clone;
    - `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` needs the whole workspace's `dist`.

    CI runs both.
  - `--ran` reconciliation: `53 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 51 run, 2 NOT-MEASURED`, `0 UNRUN`.
- `pnpm lint` (eslint over the repo): exit 0, no findings.
- **Declared narrowing:** the whole `@objectstack/runtime` `local` suite was not run here. It reads about 1000 s in CI. The diff is one self-contained test file that shares no state with its siblings. `Test Core` runs the full suite.
- No ablation: no tested behaviour changes. The before and after timings above are the evidence.

## No changeset (`skip-changeset`)

Only a `*.test.ts` file changes. `@objectstack/runtime`'s `files[]` is `dist`, `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`, and tsup's only entry is `src/index.ts`. I built `dist` after the final commit and searched it:
- the change's identifier `productionVerify`: 0 hits;
- control: `handleShareLinksRequest`: 2 hits.

## Acceptance notes

- **The memo reads a private member.** It reads `ShareLinkService`'s `verifyPassword` member, which is `private readonly` in TypeScript and is not exported.
  - If the member is renamed, `beforeAll` throws and names it.
  - If the service ever stops reading the verifier from that member, the memo stops applying and nothing else changes. The file gets slower again but never wrong, and the per-file timing report shows it.
- **`:334` and `:346` are implied by `:356`.** `:356` proves every refused cell equals the unknown-token answer, and the other two cases' references are among those cells. This was not acted on: merging or deleting cases is held off, and none of the three costs measurable time now.
- **A sibling file is also over the 10 s line.** `src/domains/share-links-messages-audience.test.ts` read 13.51 s in the same CI report. It mints with the same production hasher over a password matrix, so it probably has the same cause. It is not touched here: it is outside this card's file surface.
